column1: # Reviewed glossary for single LEGO part pages (consumed by import_lego_parts.py). Fix a term here and re-run the importer.
# Matching folds case and accents and treats "-", "/" and "_" as spaces, so "Trans-Clear" and "trans clear" are one phrase.
# [colors]  Rebrickable colour id<TAB>exact Rebrickable name (checked by the importer)<TAB>en<TAB>de<TAB>fr<TAB>nl<TAB>it<TAB>es<TAB>pl
#           Several phrases per cell are separated by "|"; an empty cell means "no reviewed term". The English cell holds the
#           Rebrickable/BrickLink name and the official LEGO name when they name the SAME colour. A name that two naming systems use
#           for different colours is never listed here but under [ambiguous]:
#           - "Dark Green": LEGO's official Dark Green is Rebrickable/BrickLink Green (2); BrickLink Dark Green is Rebrickable 288.
#           - "Light Gray"/"Dark Gray"/"hellgrau"/"dunkelgrau": the old greys (7, 8) and the 2004+ bluish greys (71, 72) are different
#             colours, and casual sellers use the plain words for both. Only explicit forms count: "light bluish gray", "medium stone
#             grey", "neuhellgrau" -> 71; "old light gray", "althellgrau" -> 7. "neu hellgrau" (two words) is not listed because
#           Base words (rot, blau, gelb, grün, schwarz, weiß, orange, beige) name the basic colour of the same BrickLink name.
# [ambiguous] One phrase per line. A title that contains one of these (or a colour modifier such as trans, metallic, pearl) outside a
#           recognised colour phrase gets no colour: the listing goes to the colour-less page instead of a guessed one.
# [part words] English part-name word<TAB>de<TAB>fr<TAB>nl<TAB>it<TAB>es<TAB>pl: search words for part pages. They extend the [words]
#           of lego_title_glossary.tsv for part names (this file wins on a shared key). Search words only, never matching aliases.
